The only pilot-derived numbers the paper may quote are the design.* and mde.* keys (pre-registered detectable gaps, results/mde.json).
_meta.source: rebuilt in memory from pilot logs with analyze.py functions (family entry rule waived)

fig1.caption: Figure 1. Summary card. What was tested, the headline price result (names associated with Black minus White buyers, in dollars per purchase, per 1,000 purchases and per $1 million of agent spend), the smallest price gap the test can reliably detect (a design number fixed before the main run) and three actions for a payments network. Audit cost is the pre-run batch estimate (COST_ESTIMATE.md). PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

fig2.caption: Figure 2. Design and where it sits in a card payment. Top: an agent purchase on a card network; the account name travels with the purchase, and the proposed audit tests the agent before it joins the network's agent program and after each model update. Bottom: one test run. The agent sees an account profile, one of three request types and one page of 8 real products, then asks a question or buys. Only the account name changes between runs; request, page, product order and replies are held fixed. Prices are from the real page hair_shampoo_fine_straight__S. Process adapted from Khaki and Choi (2026), with a one-page store in the style of WebShop (Yao et al. 2022) and ACES (Allouah et al. 2025).

fig3.caption: Figure 3. Average price paid per purchase for the same clear request (S0, no budget), by name group, on the confirmatory models. Dots: mean over names of the dollar price after removing task, wording and order effects (so every group is compared on the same task mix); bars: 95% CI across names (Claude Haiku 5.5: 4 to 5 names per group). Dashed line: average price of the cheapest product that fit the request on the same tasks. The tests of these differences are in Figure 4. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

fig4.caption: Figure 4. Confirmatory price tests (Holm correction across 4 tests). Dots: gap in price paid for the same request, focal group minus comparison group: names associated with Black minus White buyers (H1) and women minus men (H2), name-level OLS with HC2 errors; bars: 95% CI. Blue ticks: the detectable gap fixed before the main run (1.4% for H1 on Haiku, after Holm): a true gap this size would be flagged at least 80% of the time. Dotted lines: equivalence margin. Right: the same gap in dollars per purchase, per 1,000 purchases (at the comparison group's average price paid) and per $1 million of agent spend; these translate the percent gap and are not separate tests. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

fig5.caption: Figure 5. Method checks, run before any group result was examined (PLAN 8). A: a planted 'always buy the lowest-priced product that meets the request' preference for 5 names; each line is one planted name (colored by name group), clear request vs the same request with the saved preference, on the same tasks, wordings and orders; black line: their average. B: with the planted names' preference runs swapped into the clear-request data, the frozen H1 test's estimate and 95% CI vs the expected diluted gap (planted shift x 5 / 20); PLAN 8.1 requires the CI to cover it, and detection only when the swapped data's own detectable gap says it should be found. C: 'best quality' minus 'cheapest that fits' per name (small marks) and on average (large mark). D: share of 1,000 label shuffles with p < 0.05 for each confirmatory test (limit 8.5%; above it the test switches to its permutation p-value). Panels without data in these runs are left out. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

fig6.caption: Figure 6. Hair and skin tasks, by name group. A to C: vague requests where the buyer's need was hidden and the agent bought without asking. A: share of picks that fit the hidden need. B and C: wrong-product (other need) rate split by the buyer's actual need, never pooled, since a guess from a name hurts buyers whose need does not match the guess and those errors cancel in a pooled number. D and E: clear requests that stated the need; share of picks that went against the stated need, split by that need. F (exploratory, descriptive): dollars spent on the wrong product per 1,000 vague purchases, the wrong-product rate times the average price paid in that cell, by actual need. Dots: mean over names; bars: 95% CI across names. H3 tests the identity-linked pick when the need is stated, and H4 the same pick in the A to C runs, both names associated with Black minus White buyers; H4's detectable gap after Holm is 11.5 points. H4 conditions on not asking, so the ask rate (Figure 7) belongs beside it. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

fig7.caption: Figure 7. Share of runs where the agent asked the buyer a question (top) and where it did not complete a purchase (bottom), by request type and name group; dots: mean over names, bars: 95% CI across names. Exploratory; tests controlled at a 10% false discovery rate, and q is printed only where q < 0.10. No purchase includes refusals, errors, invalid product IDs and no tool call. In vague requests the agent could ask twice before a scripted 'choose one yourself' reply (Deviation D1); runs logged before D1 keep one answered ask. Second-ask rates are in the CSV. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

figA1.caption: Figure A1. Position bias (PLAN 10 Figure A1, same computation as analyze.py). Share of purchases at each displayed position, forward vs reversed product order, arms S0, S1 and V pooled; dashed line: 12.5%, no position preference. The product order is part of every test cell, so position is held fixed by design. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

figA2.caption: Figure A2. Price paid vs the no-name buyer, by name group and request type (PLAN 10 Figure 1, same computation as analyze.py). Dots: group mean of name averages after removing task, wording and order effects, minus the no-name accounts' mean, as percent; bars: Welch 95% CI across names. Dotted lines in the clear-request panel: the detectable gap after Holm. Hispanic and Asian cells are exploratory. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.

figA4.caption: Figure A4. Gaps by model and outcome (focal group minus comparison group, name level, 95% CI); price in percent, rates in percentage points. Blue ticks: detectable gap after Holm where pre-registered. Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna are confirmatory when they enter the family (PLAN 3); Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and OLMo 3 7B are exploratory, shown as estimates only (open markers). The two right columns are exploratory tests (Benjamini-Hochberg, 10%). One model version per vendor on one date. PILOT DATA, NOT RESULTS.
